Define $\mathcal E_K\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ to consist of all pairs $(M,L)$ for which some representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has a common invariant line on which $\rho(\mu)$ acts by $M$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ acts by $L$. The Zariski closure is the smallest Zariski-closed algebraic subset containing $\mathcal E_K$; let $V_K$ be the union of its one-dimensional irreducible components, where an irreducible component is a maximal irreducible closed subset. Zero-dimensional image components are omitted. The **ordinary A-polynomial** $A_K(M,L)$ is the Laurent polynomial generating the vanishing ideal of $V_K$, chosen square-free (no repeated irreducible factors) and with primitive integer coefficients (their greatest common divisor is one). It is determined up to multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$ for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$. Its reduced curve includes the abelian component $L=1$; equivalently, its representative in $\mathbb Z[M,L]$ is divisible by $L-1$.
